items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But when he was a leader, and I played with him at 16 years old

ctx.x: Well, my father taught schnorrers how to be classy musicians. He taught common people, common musicians, you know you’re talking about people who escaped from Russia like my father did — they all — and you know any musician my father ever hired it was like the Monday night Birdland jazz jam sessions where when you got there you were hired, you never really knew who you were going to play with — because no music, we all knew the same — we just played all the same songs. My father would have — he was a bandleader,…

with my father he couldn’t be drunk on the job. But when he was a leader, and I played with him at 16 years old, you see what I wrote about him, I can’t say it on our show here, but you’ll see I wrote what he said to me.
